survey.architecture: FastAPI is a modern web framework built on top of Starlette for building high-performance HTTP APIs with automatic validation, serialization, and OpenAPI documentation. It provides a decorator-based routing system combined with a dependency injection framework that analyzes function signatures to automatically extract, validate, and inject request data (query parameters, path parameters, headers, cookies, request bodies) and dependencies. The framework is organized around three main layers: the application layer (FastAPI class extending Starlette), the routing layer (APIRouter and APIRoute classes), and a dependency resolution layer that uses Pydantic for validation.

entry_points.what_it_starts: The main FastAPI application class that developers import and instantiate to create web applications. Extends Starlette with routing decorators and dependency injection.
CLI entry point when FastAPI module is run as a script (python -m fastapi). Delegates to CLI implementation in fastapi.cli.
Command-line interface for FastAPI, providing commands for running servers and managing applications via Typer CLI framework.

core_abstractions.role: Main application class that users interact with. Extends Starlette and provides decorator-based routing methods (get, post, etc.), middleware management, OpenAPI documentation, and dependency injection setup.
Route handler class that wraps an endpoint function, manages dependency resolution, request validation, response serialization, and handles both HTTP and WebSocket endpoints.
Reusable routing component that collects routes and can be included in a FastAPI app, supporting the same decorator-based API as FastAPI itself.
Represents an analyzed callable (function or dependency) with its parameters, sub-dependencies, security requirements, and caching metadata extracted from the function signature.
Base class for parameter metadata that annotates function parameters to define where request data comes from (path, query, header, cookie, body, form, file) and validation rules.
Exception class for raising HTTP errors with status code and detail message, caught by default exception handler and converted to JSON responses.
Core function that resolves and validates all dependencies for an endpoint by extracting values from request (query params, body, headers, etc.) and recursively solving sub-dependencies.

steps.what_happens: Developer instantiates FastAPI app and sets up title, description, routes, middleware, and exception handlers.
Developer decorates a handler function with @app.get('/path') to register an endpoint with HTTP method, path, response model, and other OpenAPI metadata.
Route decorator creates APIRoute instance that analyzes the handler function signature to extract path parameters, dependencies, body schema, response schema using dependency injection analysis.
During route initialization, analyzes endpoint function to extract all parameters, detect which are path/query/header/body/form/file based on annotations, and build Dependant object.
Creates the actual ASGI app callable that will handle incoming requests, setting up dependency injection, body parsing, validation, and response serialization logic.
When HTTP request arrives, the inner 'app' function is called with the Request object and AsyncExitStack for resource cleanup.
Request body is parsed (JSON, form data, or raw bytes) based on Content-Type header and route configuration.
All route parameters and dependencies are validated and extracted from request (path params, query params, headers, cookies, body) using Pydantic validation, recursively resolving sub-dependencies.
Handler function is called with resolved dependency values as keyword arguments. If sync function, it runs in thread pool; if async, awaited directly.
Response from handler is serialized using response_model if provided, applying Pydantic validation and jsonable_encoder to convert Python objects to JSON-compatible types.
Response is wrapped in response class (default JSONResponse), background tasks are attached, and response is returned to ASGI server.
Developer marks a function parameter with Depends(some_dependency) to declare a sub-dependency that should be resolved and injected.
During route initialization, get_dependant analyzes handler function and creates a Dependant tree where dependencies are collected recursively.
Flattens the dependency tree into a linear list of all dependencies with their execution order and cache keys for deduplication.
At request time, iterates through flat dependency list, calls each dependency function or generator, caches results by cache key to prevent duplicate calls, handles cleanup of generators.
Once all dependencies are resolved and cached, endpoint function is called with complete values dict containing all parameters and resolved dependencies.

steps.what_happens: When /openapi.json is requested or docs are being generated, openapi() method is called to generate the OpenAPI specification.

For each route, extracts operation metadata (method, path, summary, description, tags) and builds parameter/request/response definitions from Dependant and response_model.
Extracts query, path, header, and cookie parameters from route dependencies and converts them to OpenAPI parameter objects with validation constraints.
Creates OpenAPI request body schema from the body field/model, including validation constraints and examples.
Internal routes for /docs and /redoc are registered to serve Swagger UI and ReDoc documentation pages.
When /docs is accessed, returns HTML page that loads Swagger UI and initializes it with the OpenAPI spec from /openapi.json.

boundaries.note: Extends starlette.applications.Starlette, building on Starlette's ASGI application framework, middleware stack, and exception handling. FastAPI adds routing decorators, dependency injection, and OpenAPI generation.

Security schemes are implemented as Dependant-compatible callables that can be used as dependencies, extracting and validating credentials from requests and raising HTTPException on failure.
Parameter types can be subclassed to create custom parameter extractors that integrate with the dependency injection system and are analyzed by get_dependant.
Exception handlers are registered in FastAPI.__init__ and can be overridden or extended by users to customize how exceptions are converted to HTTP responses.
APIRoute can be subclassed and passed as route_class parameter to customize route behavior, parameter extraction, or response handling.
Automatically added middleware that manages async context managers and resource cleanup by injecting AsyncExitStack into request scope for handler access.
Converts Python objects (dates, decimals, enums, Pydantic models, dataclasses) to JSON-serializable types, used before passing responses to JSON encoder.
Wraps starlette.datastructures.UploadFile, extending it with Pydantic schema generation for automatic OpenAPI documentation of file upload parameters.

core_abstractions.role: Wraps endpoint functions with automatic dependency injection, request validation (via Pydantic), and response serialization. Routes HTTP requests to validated and resolved handlers.

Returns the handler function (get_request_handler) that will process this request, created during route registration.
Creates an ASGI app that: (1) extracts the Request object, (2) solves all dependencies, (3) calls endpoint with resolved args, (4) validates and serializes response.
Walks Dependant graph, extracts parameter values from request (path, query, body, etc.), validates via Pydantic, handles security checks, returns injection dict.
Encodes endpoint return value to JSON bytes via Pydantic serialization, wrapping in HTTPResponse with appropriate headers.
Decorator method (POST, PUT, DELETE, etc. are similar) that registers a path-operation endpoint with GET method.
Creates APIRoute instance with endpoint function, methods, status codes, and metadata.
Analyzes endpoint function via get_dependant, extracts return type annotation, builds OpenAPI operation metadata, stores handler.
Inspects endpoint signature: identifies path params, query params, body fields, security dependencies, and sub-dependencies via Depends() markers.
At app initialization, walks all routes and their Dependants to generate OpenAPI schema served at /docs.
Decorator marking a parameter as a dependency: wraps callable in Param with is_dependency=True.
During route registration, detects Depends() markers and recursively analyzes dependency functions to build dependency tree.
At request time, recursively resolves all dependencies: calls each dependency callable (possibly with its own nested dependencies), caches results by scope.
Calls the endpoint function with resolved dependency values injected as keyword arguments.

boundaries.note: FastAPI extends Starlette; users create FastAPI instances and call .get()/.post()/etc. to register routes, or use .include_router() to compose APIs.
APIRoute wraps user endpoint functions; users write async/sync functions and FastAPI introspects them to extract parameters and dependencies.
Depends() marks parameters as injectable dependencies; users write dependency callables and inject them into handlers and other dependencies.
Base class for security schemes; FastAPI provides API key, HTTP, OAuth2, OpenID Connect implementations; users can subclass to add custom schemes.
Users can register custom exception handlers to catch and transform exceptions into responses.
Users can add ASGI middleware to the application to intercept and transform requests/responses.
Pydantic v2 integration: FastAPI abstracts Pydantic v2 field handling for request validation and response serialization via ModelField compatibility shim.
Starlette dependency: FastAPI inherits from starlette.applications.Starlette and uses its routing, middleware, and ASGI handling.
Uses Starlette's request/response ASGI handling; calls starlette.concurrency for thread pool operations on blocking code.
Generates OpenAPI 3.0.0 schema; served as JSON and rendered via external Swagger UI / ReDoc endpoints (served from openapi/docs.py).

entry_points.what_it_starts: The FastAPI application lifecycle. Constructor initializes the ASGI app with routes, middleware, and documentation. __call__ delegates ASGI requests to the middleware stack and router.
CLI entry point from fastapi.cli module, allowing command-line invocation of the framework.
HTTP request handler creation, returning an async function that validates requests, resolves dependencies, executes the endpoint function, and serializes the response.

Low-level request handler factory that coordinates request body parsing, dependency resolution via solve_dependencies, endpoint execution, and response serialization for both standard and streaming responses.

core_abstractions.role: Core dependency model that represents an endpoint or dependency function with its parameters (path, query, header, cookie, body, dependencies) and metadata (OAuth scopes, caching). Used by routing and dependency resolution.

Core route abstraction extending Starlette Route, representing a single path operation with its endpoint function, validation metadata, response model, and OpenAPI configuration. Generates request handlers via get_route_handler.
Main application class extending Starlette, orchestrating route registration, middleware stacking, dependency injection, exception handling, and OpenAPI schema generation.
Core function that executes the dependency injection graph: validates request data, resolves all dependencies recursively, calls their functions, and returns solved values for endpoint injection.
Base parameter descriptor class extending Pydantic FieldInfo, used by all parameter types (Query, Path, Body, Header, Cookie, Form, File) to annotate endpoint parameters.

steps.what_happens: ASGI entry point receives scope/receive/send, sets root_path, delegates to parent Starlette.__call__ which routes through middleware stack.
Places two AsyncExitStacks in request scope (fastapi_middleware_astack for file cleanup, fastapi_inner_astack for dependency cleanup), allowing proper resource finalization.
Creates and returns the actual async request handler function that will process this specific route's requests.
The returned handler parses the request body (form or JSON), validates content-type, catches JSON decode errors as RequestValidationError.
Validates request path/query/header/cookie/body parameters against the Dependant's field definitions, recursively resolves sub-dependencies, executes dependency functions with injected values.
Executes the endpoint function with values from solve_dependencies, handling both sync and async callables, wrapping sync functions to run in thread pool.
Validates response data against response_model if present, serializes to JSON via jsonable_encoder, handles streaming responses (SSE, JSONL), and wraps in Response object.
Catches RequestValidationError during dependency solving, formats errors as JSON with 422 status code.

flows.name: Route Registration and OpenAPI Generation Flow

steps.what_happens: Accepts endpoint callable, creates APIRoute with validation config, adds to router's routes list.
Calls get_dependant to analyze the endpoint function signature and extract all parameters and dependencies.
Inspects endpoint signature, calls analyze_param for each parameter to identify parameter type (path/query/body/depends), builds Dependant with parameter lists and dependency tree.
Stores dependant, response_model, OpenAPI metadata, generates unique operation ID, compiles path regex for matching.
Calls get_openapi with all routes to generate OpenAPI 3.0+ schema, caches result in openapi_schema.
Iterates routes, extracts parameters and models via get_openapi_path, builds complete OpenAPI spec with paths, schemas, security definitions.
Registers internal routes for /openapi.json (OpenAPI schema), /docs (Swagger UI), /redoc (ReDoc) if enabled.
When analyzing a parameter annotated with Security(scheme), creates a sub-Dependant for the security scheme with its OAuth scopes.
Traverses dependency tree, for each Dependant calls request_params_to_args and request_body_to_args to extract validated values from request.
Validates path, query, header, cookie parameters against their ModelFields, handling aliases and validation errors.
Security scheme callable that extracts token from Authorization header, raises 403 if missing (triggering not_authenticated_error handler).
Collects all solved values and errors, wraps with AsyncExitStack for cleanup, returns SolvedDependency with values dict and errors list.

boundaries.note: Extends Starlette.applications.Starlette for ASGI app handling, routing infrastructure, middleware support, and exception handling. FastAPI is built on top of Starlette.
Pydantic v2 (or v1 via compatibility shim) field models used for request validation. FastAPI abstracts Pydantic version differences via _compat layer.
Dependency overrides can be injected via dependency_overrides_provider parameter, allowing test mocks and runtime overrides of any dependency.
Applications can register custom exception handlers via decorator or add_exception_handler, allowing domain-specific error responses.
Applications can add custom middleware via decorator, allowing custom processing of requests/responses and contextvars manipulation.
Routers can be included in the main app or nested, allowing modular route organization and prefix-based path composition.
Custom route classes can override get_route_handler to provide alternate request handling logic.
Applications can override openapi() method to customize OpenAPI schema generation or provide alternate documentation.
Dependency injection is declared via Depends parameter, which can reference callables defined anywhere in user code, enabling arbitrary dependency graphs.
OAuth2 security schemes are defined via Security(scheme, scopes=[...]), allowing pluggable authentication/authorization logic.
